title: Coding a 2D sidescroller?
author: juni030
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I want to surprise my sons with a custom 16-bit side-scrolling runner game that has a classic Super Nintendo vibe.

I currently have access to Gemini Pro (using Google AI Studio for the larger context window), but I don't have the new Argon model. Since I can't rely on Argon's agentic coding features to handle the project autonomously, I need to guide Gemini Pro step-by-step.

For those of you who have coded games with Pro:

What is the most stable environment to ask for? (I was thinking a single-file HTML5 Canvas approach?)

How do you structure your prompts to build the core physics first before adding sprite animations?

How do you prevent the AI from losing track or breaking the code as the game gets more complex?

Any advice, prompt templates, or workflow tips would be hugely appreciated!

comments.author: SimoneNonvelodico
comments.body:
I use Claude, not Gemini, but what I can say about the questions in general:

1. HTML5+Canvas is definitely the most easily portable option, and one the AI will be very familiar with. Consider suggesting an engine for rendering (PixiJS) or even for the game as a whole (Phaser). That'll save you on a lot of foundational code that could go wrong.

2. I would suggest telling the AI your general idea and to start by building with placeholders, then tell it to add the sprite animations etc separately. If you use an engine as above most of the tools are already there.

3. Try keeping things modular and decoupled, same as with human development. Tell it how systems should be able to stand on their own and see other APIs as black boxes. For this kind of game honestly it shouldn't be a big deal, it's small/simple enough.

comments.author: the_builder_ai
comments.body:
https://reddit.com/link/1xhp6mz/video/gpk45ley08yh1/player

I use Claude + ChatGPT and if this is the kind of side scroller effect that you are working for:

1) "I want to build a 2.5D side scroller game with \[style/theme\]" - I came across this somewhere (not made by me or not affiliated at all but simply thought it could be useful: [https://gameartstyle.loopyhop.com/?category=pixel](https://gameartstyle.loopyhop.com/?category=pixel) ). This gives the foundation of your game. I also like to think of a general size of the play field. For example, each stretch can be 500 M or longer or shorter depending. You can also consider vertical canvas - how much jumping upward movement you want. Other things to consider: Whether you want weather effect? Foreground vs. background? Without more info of what you like it is hard for me to give you a specific prompt but you can play around with the specifics.

2) I would start with having a general feel of the map before getting proper character. Initial playtest with procedurally generated character is fine. Once you have a better basis you can start to use image gen like ChatGPT or others to make sprites and animate your character

3) In general, no need to worry about AI losing track or breaking code. But I would definitely get a md file in place to log all the edits that you have made each session and version so you can always have fallback and reference.

I'm posting a devlog/tips as I work through so feel free to follow along or ask me any questions. [https://x.com/thepaulymarket](https://x.com/thepaulymarket)

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: single-file html is fine but i'd ask gemini for phaser 3 (loaded from a cdn) instead of raw canvas, it gives you arcade physics and sprite animations for free so the ai isn't reinventing gravity every time. build it in small steps (runner + jump with colored boxes first, then obstacles, then sprites) and paste the whole current file back in each time so it doesn't lose track. for a feel of a pixel-art runner built that way, vampire strider is a phaser one made mostly with ai: [https://vibe1up.com/game/vampire-strider/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=comment&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://vibe1up.com/game/vampire-strider/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=comment&utm_campaign=aigamedev) (i run that site, it checks every game's link daily and keeps dead ones as archived offline pages so whatever you click actually works)
